passage: Literature often reflects the values and concerns of the societies in which it is written. Novels, poems, and plays can reveal attitudes about politics, culture, and human relationships during a particular historical period. For this reason, historians sometimes study literature alongside official historical records. While factual documents provide concrete information about events, literary works offer insight into how people felt and interpreted those events. Together, these sources create a more complete understanding of history and human experience.
